requirements.note: All 260 tickers listed with symbol, name, price and % since open, green when up and red when down (system green/red, adapts in dark mode).
About 20 prices change each second. Rows update in place, also while scrolled mid-list. Under price/change sort, rows re-sort live.
Native pull-down menu: Symbol A–Z, Price highest first, Change highest first (no way to reverse the order). Bottom-toolbar search matches symbol ('hm') and name ('cedar'), with a proper empty state.
Star toggles fill and accessibility label. A native segmented control switches All / My List.
Inset-grouped detail screen shows name, large price, change, open and volume, and a live 60-sample line chart with low/high. History builds up from app launch.
My List (HMX, DXI) and Price sort survived a relaunch.

bugs: Under price or change sort, live re-ordering moves rows under the finger: starring two adjacent rows in a row starred HMX instead of the intended RZC because the list had re-sorted between taps.
tells: Inline title only; no large title on the root list
No swipe actions on rows (star/unstar by swipe)
At the largest text size, rows switch to a stacked layout with a very large star sitting alone on its own line above the symbol; it works but looks oversized
The sort menu cannot reverse the order (e.g. lowest price first)
A.scroll: Smooth native collection-view scrolling with system bounce; fling and fling-back worked with no blank rows or pop-in. Live updates and re-sorting kept going during scrolling without visible jumps beyond the expected re-ordering.

requirements.note: All 260 tickers with symbol, name, price and change. Change is shown as a green/red tinted pill badge.
Prices update every second, in place, including while scrolled. Under change sort, rows re-sort live.
Native menu with Symbol/Price/Change plus a Descending-order toggle. In-list search field matches symbol and name, with a 'No matches' empty state and a Clear search button.
Star toggles, and a segmented control switches All / My List.
Detail screen shows price, % and $ change, open, volume (7.73M plus exact share count), window high/low, and a live area chart with a LIVE badge and time axis.
My List (ZEXO) and Change-descending sort survived a relaunch.

bugs: A horizontal swipe on a row opens the detail screen as if it were a tap, instead of doing nothing or revealing swipe actions
Under change sort, live re-ordering moves rows under the finger while browsing
tells: Custom-themed look: navy-tinted text, a bespoke green accent and off-white background instead of system label colours and tint; reads more like a web/fintech design than a stock iOS list
Search is a hand-placed rounded text field inside the list header that scrolls away, not a system search bar or .searchable field (no Cancel button, no toolbar search)
Change values are drawn as custom tinted pills rather than plain coloured text
Rows are 83 pt tall, so only about 6 rows fit; the header (status line, segmented control, search, count, sort) uses a third of the screen
At the largest text size the row star and the search placeholder do not scale, and the 'Every second' label disappears
On the detail screen, the 'Open' label/value is not baseline-aligned with the 'Volume' block next to it
B.scroll: Scrolling is smooth with a native bounce and large-title collapse, and no blank rows after a fling. The tall rows mean a lot of flinging to cover 260 tickers, and live re-sorting shuffles rows while browsing.

why: Both apps meet all six requirements and persist state. A looks and behaves like a stock iOS 26/27 SwiftUI app: system colours, toolbar search, a native menu, a native segmented control, a dense list and an inset-grouped detail screen. B adds nice extras (a sort-direction toggle, a richer chart, window high/low), but its custom theme, scroll-away hand-placed search field, pill badges, tall rows and swipe-opens-detail behaviour give it away as not hand-built for iOS.
